notes.title: Star Racer, a combat ship speedfest about evading the fuzz as an alien M.O.M, has zoomed out of early access
notes.notes:
Steam's in the midst of a racing fest at the moment, and as you can probably imagine if you've not taken to tuning out the litany of driving-related words I've carved into the tree that houses the esteemed RPS treehouse in the short time I've been here thus far (believe me, I don't blame you if you have), I'm in my element.

One of the games I've spotted as a result of this celebration of all things car-ish is Star Racer, which doesn't involve cars at all. It's a retro-style ship racer that lets you blast your fellow competitors to bits, feels very much inspired by the likes of F-Zero and Wipeout, and just emerged from early access the other day.

Read more

notes.title: Star Racer 1.0 Release
notes.notes:
[h1]It’s official. We’re finally at our 1.0 release!!![/h1][p]
[/p][p]Star Racer really would not be what it is today without so much help and support from so many people. Thank you to the many talented musicians who helped create an incredible soundtrack. Thank you to all the engineers who helped translate our design vision into reality. Thank you to all the artists who helped bring this world and these characters to life. Thank you to our friends and family for their unwavering and unending support. Thank you to our Kickstarter backers who put faith into this project when it was just a fledgling demo.[/p][p]
[/p][p]I have a couple of house keeping notes I also want to mention.[/p][p]
[/p][h2]Updated Price: [/h2][p]In case you missed our previous announcement, the new official price of the game is [b][i]$9.99[/i][/b]. All Kickstarter backers who backed the project at the original price will be receiving a copy of Soundtrack at no additional cost.[/p][p]
[/p][h2]Steam Racing Fest: [/h2][p]We are a part of this sale and are providing a [b][i]20%[/i][/b] discount, making the game [b][i]$7.99[/i][/b] for first-time buyers. The sale will be active for 2 weeks.[/p][p]
[/p][h2]Kickstarter Perks: [/h2][p]There are two remaining perks that are still work-in-progress: The Soundtrack and the Kickstarter Vehicle Color Palette. Now that we’ve made the 1.0 release we can now return to working on these perks. We will update you all with release dates soon. Make sure to join our Discord as we provide more in-progress updates there! Besides these two, all of the other perks have been completed — including the Credits, which you can find under Collections in the main menu.[/p][p]
[/p][h2]Demo: [/h2][p]We have updated the demo! So if you are still unsure, but want to rock out to a few tracks by [i][b]Grant Kirkhope, Mason Lieberman, and Jules Conroy[/b][/i]... (and myself) while testing out the driving mechanics, give the new demo a try! You can even compete on the death race leaderboards.[/p][p][/p][h2]
Final Thoughts:[/h2][p]It feels so good that we were able to get to this day. But this 1.0 release is just the beginning. We have planned work to fix bugs and optimize the game. There are many more features we want to bring to Star Racer (yes, including online multiplayer), more platforms we want to be on. We will be actively reaching out to more partners and publishers to make Star Racer as great as it can be. [/p][p]
[/p][p]And this is just the beginning of Whatnot Games. There are so many types of games we want to make, and we are so thankful that so many of you have already joined us on our journey. We hope that you’ll continue to watch us as we try to make games that we wished existed in the world.[/p][p]
[/p][p]So please spread the word. Leave reviews (good or bad, but preferably good!). And report bugs. It’s time to get to work. See you on the track, racers![/p][p][/p][p][i]-- Brennan Anderson[/i][/p]

notes.title: Star Racer v0.9.0
notes.notes: [p]Hi Everybody! Today we are releasing version 0.9.0. We are in the end game! At this point, the game is [b]mostly[/b] feature complete. The last few things we are working on are the final few event races, a few UI screens, bug fixes, and optimization. [/p][p][/p][p]The newest feature of this update is the new CPU behavior system. We re-wrote it, and it can handle most tracks so much better than before, and there is more of a sense of tension when fighting a vehicle for 1st place. Now, this is the first public release of it, so there are going to be some issues, so please don't hesitate to post about them either on Steam, or on our Discord! We are going to be fixing and polishing up as much as we can these last few weeks before the 1.0 release.[/p][p][/p][p]Now, one thing that I know a lot of people will notice is the performance if you are not on a beefy machine. We are not done optimizing the game yet. We know that on several tracks, there are major performance dips (most notably Cosmo Casino and Holographic Highway). We have a few tricks up our sleeves and will be addressing that as much as we can by 1.0, but there is also a possibility it will be a patch very shortly after 1.0.[/p][p][/p][p]Please, please, please, report any and all bugs you find, let us know how the CPU behaviors feel as we work on them a bit more. We are aiming to make this launch as good as possible, and we need your help and support to do that. [/p][p][/p][p]Thank you so much![/p][p]-- Brennan[/p]

notes.title: Star Racer Major Update v0.8.1
notes.notes:
[h1]Steam Workshop Integration[/h1][p]Let's get right to the biggest part of this update; Steam Workshop Integration. We have put in a lot of work making sure that the workshop integration is as seamless as possible for players. [/p][p][/p][p]It starts off in the course editor. Once you make a track, you must complete one lap on the test track to make sure that the course is completable. Then you may upload to the workshop straight from the editor screen. You may also make changes and update your workshop item at any time (you have to complete one lap any time you make a change!). Once the course is uploaded, you will get the workshop info panel on the left. You may then open the steam overlay to make any changes to the item description.[/p][p][/p][p]In the course select screen, you have the option to open the workshop in the Steam overlay. This is how you can browse and subscribe to other player's courses! The new courses should download very quickly (the largest file size I've seen is less than half a MB), and the course will appear in the carousel as soon as it is downloaded.

So, give the workshop a try! Show people what you can make, challenge your friends, or troll them with devious courses. Have fun pushing the course editor o its limits! Every official course that we made in the game was made using the exact same tools in the course editor. It was very important to me that anything we can make, the players can make too. There are no hidden developer features in terms of what you can create in the editor.[/p][p][/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679155/58d3915c42b46f9f0f257debe304e96a848d864a.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679155/032499a0f63503dbc182db5297cd6f355931f2e8.png"][/img][/carousel][h1]Version Number Readjustment[/h1][p]Ok, so I was really bad at estimating how long things would take and what features constituted a major/minor/patch version. That was my bad. But, no time like the present to correct that. We have updated the version number to 0.8.1 at the time of this writing. 0.8 is the inclusion of Steam Workshop integration, and we patched it with some minor bug fixes. On our roadmap, we have one more major feature planned for the 0.9.0 release, then a bunch of polish/tuning/bug fixes before we get to the 1.0.0 version. We are nearing the end![/p][p][/p][h1]Features/Tuning Changes[/h1][p][/p][h2]Accessibility Settings[/h2][p]This one has been a long time coming, and I was finally able to dedicate some time to it. All of the settings aren't completed, but two major features are done, and those are the one hand modes and auto acceleration. [/p][p][/p][h3]Auto Acceleration[/h3][p]Auto acceleration is fairly self-explanatory, it allows you not to have to worry about holding the acceleration button. Braking overrides acceleration, and tapping acceleration still performs drift boosts.[/p][p][/p][h3]One Hand Mode[/h3][p]This was inspired by my cousin who broke his hand and was having a hard time playing the game. It reinforced the idea that many disabilities are temporary, and that shouldn't preclude you from enjoying a game. One Hand Mode does what it says, it allows you to play the game with one hand. There are some drawbacks to that, as we are using most of the buttons on the controller already, but I think it works well enough. [/p][p][/p][p]Type 1 maps the acceleration and braking to up and down on the right analogue stick with pressing in to boost. Attacks are on the shoulder buttons. Strafing is on the face buttons.[/p][p][/p][p]Type 2 maps the acceleration and braking to the shoulder buttons. Strafing and attacks are on the face buttons.[/p][p][/p][p]Both types will side dash and spin in the direction you are turning. Both types are ambidextrous, so you can play with either hand since controllers are for the most part pretty symmetrical.[/p][p][/p][p]When you combine One Hand Mode, Auto Acceleration, and options to invert both horizontal and vertical axes, my hope is that there are powerful and robust enough accessibility settings so that anybody can play this game.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679155/80c63dbf12c8bc8b66cee2d9de4048fd863ce3fc.png"][/img][/p][h2]Rank Badges[/h2][p]I think the game was really missing some incentives to play the different game modes. Sure they are fun, and yes you unlock characters by doing them, but it wasn't feeling sticky enough. So now we have added rank badges that you can collect for doing well on most game modes. They will be prominently displayed with that game mode. This includes Grand Prix, Time Trials, Death Race, and Event Races. Now you can collect as many S-Rank Badges as you can and show them off to friends! There is some light shaming involved too. You can get down to a D-Rank if you don't do particularly well. We opted not to give an F-Rank at least![/p][p][/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679155/02bd84a1d07abf6c6fedd2638e560b708827581b.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679155/f1e7250e42a9cf32655375807351fd612f163b19.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679155/7141f6365e9fde07fb996b7cb1499d5b7f24cddf.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679155/89897a8c4f0c40a64c2414f8d7a31bc63e504c4e.png"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][h2]Other Features[/h2][p]Here is a short list of the other notable features we have added:[/p][list][*][p]Boost Checkpoints. Now on point-to-point races, you can add a boost checkpoint. This will enable the boost power for the rest of the race.[/p][/*][*][p]Tons of new VO from our announcer! Including all the characters, and some in-race flavor lines![/p][/*][*][p]Precision Boost Pads. There is a new boost pad type that will rotate your vehicle to orient in the direction of the boost pad.[/p][/*][*][p]Boost Chaining. Boosts are now more technical, as they don't automatically put you up to your top speed anymore. They dow increase your speed a bit, but not as fast. So to get to your top speed quickly you have to chain multiple boosts together. When hitting a boost pad after you already manually boosted, you will get to the top speed even faster, and every time you hit another boost pad before your previous boost runs out, your max boost speed will increase a bit. This will let you reach super high speeds on some courses if you have the skill to hit all of the boost pads.[/p][/*][*][p]Allowing retry in every game mode, including event races.[/p][/*][*][p]Added Wildlands course (Designed by Silent Fox).[/p][/*][*][p]Added Planet Core course (Designed by Silent Fox).[/p][/*][*][p]At least 10 unlock-able color palettes for each character.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]Bug Fixes[/h1][p]Too many to count, like seriously. My work style is that I fix bugs as fast as I make them. So as many features are in the game, many more than that amount of bugs have been fixed. Here are a few notable ones though.[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Fixed mouse cursor not clicking on buttons in the course editor when using Mouse and Keyboard controls (that was a fun one)[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed tutorials freezing on start.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed not being able to lock on to targets and turrets[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed homing laser rapidly spinning around you infinitely[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed wind not rendering properly[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Star Racer 1.0 Launch Date and Pricing Announcement
notes.notes:
[h1]1.0 Launch Date[/h1]

Hello everybody!  You may have heard the news today that Star Racer is leaving early access on July 28th!  If you haven't heard, please check out the trailer here:

[url=https://youtu.be/fH-0v81pFms?si=r9mpYEXqKAGAnjqI]1.0 Launch Date Trailer[/url]

We are super excited to show off all of the hard work we have done, and can't wait for you all to play it. Of course, you can play it now if you really want, but please keep reading before you do.

[h1]Launch Price[/h1]
Once Star Racer launches to it's 1.0 version, we will be permanently decreasing the price to $9.99. Why are we doing this? Is it because the game is hot garbage and we are hoping to pull the wool over player's eyes? Yes, that's exactly what we are doing (cue impostor syndrome).

In all seriousness, while other companies have been raising the prices of their games and setting the industry standard to be more expensive, we see and hear a lot of gamers who are upset by that. We are upset by it too!

We know that a lot of people are struggling right now. There isn't as much disposable income as there used to be. For us, games aren't just a nice to have hobby, but an art form that we have grown passionate about both making and playing. Everybody deserves to be able to play games. Will a $5 decrease magically solve the world's problems? Probably not, but I do know that it will take a little bit of the sting away from people who want to enjoy a new game but who also have to worry about where their money is going.

To all of my Kickstarter backers and early access players who supported the game with the understanding that you were receiving the game at a specific discount, or who even paid the full $14.99: I want to thank you for your support and understanding. The world and the economy were completely different a year ago, and you generously contributed what you could. I couldn't have finished out the game without your support, and as a result we have been able to add even more features than we originally planned. Your investment of time and money made this game way better than it would have been otherwise. As a thank you, [b]we will be gifting the Star Racer Soundtrack (once it is finished) to anybody who purchases the game prior to the official 1.0 launch date[/b].

So, please wishlist the game so that you get notified when it leaves early access on July 28th. There will be a launch discount as well! For new players who are interested and really want to play, we have updated the demo to include a lot of the new gameplay.

Thank you all so much!

-- Brennan Anderson

notes.title: Star Racer 4.1 Update
notes.notes:
Hey all! We've been super hard at work on Star Racer, and we have a pretty big update for you all! 

This update includes tons of balancing changes, bug fixes, and polish updates.

[h1]Features[/h1]
[list]
[*] Time Trials: They are now basically complete! You can race to record your ghosts, and your fastest times will be uploaded to the steam leaderboards. Your best times will also be saved and counted towards unlocks for some characters.
[*] Supernova maneuver: If you manually boost immediately after executing a drift boost, you will perform a supernova. This is a huge boost in speed, and it will drop a mine behind your vehicle, damaging any other vehicle who drives through it. Be careful though, it takes a lot of energy.
[*] First Place Bombing: If you are in first place, towards the end of the race, the authorities want you to lose, so they will start shooting bombs at you! Avoid them at all costs if you want to win!
[*] Added a new track called Frozen Corkscrew.
[/list]

[h1]Balance Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Luca has slower top speed, but much faster boosts.
[*] Neon has much faster boosts, but they have dramatically slower durations
[*] Zhara has much slower top speed, but her speed scales better with capsules. At full capsules, she is one of the faster vehicles, but at no capsules she is one of the slowest.
[*] Automaton accelerates extremely fast, but also stops extremely fast as well, making it's movement all or nothing.
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Allow you to retry in the middle of time trials and quick races now works.
[*] Fixed vehicles not exiting flight mode when touching the track sometimes.

Hey Everybody!

[h2]Early Access[/h2]
Star Racer is releasing into Early Access! Why? Well, we want to get it out to as many people as possible, and we want to listen and incorporate as much feedback as we can. From vehicle tuning and difficulty settings to courses and unlock conditions, we want to know what you think, and take steps to make Star Racer as good as it possibly can be. We will also be using this time to finish developing the content and remaining game modes that will make Star Racer feel complete and super fun!

During development there are bound to be a few bugs and issues present. We have created a bug tracking spreadsheet so that you can be aware of all the known issues in the game. If you would like to report a bug, you can do so on the Steam forums, or respond to the following google form. You can also head over to the Discord server to discuss any issues as well.

notes.title: Kickstarter Campaign Ending Soon!
notes.notes:
Hey Everybody!

I hope everybody had a wonderful holiday and is getting ready for a great new year! We are in the final hours of the Kickstarter now and I want to focus on sharing what it means to me that so many people have already supported this project. If you haven't checked it out, please consider backing at the link below! If we reach the next stretch goal (we are so close), Grant Kirkhope will be writing more music for the game!

[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/whatnotgames/star-racer]https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/whatnotgames/star-racer[/url]

Some of my earliest memories with games were when my cousin and I were traveling with our families. We checked in to a hotel and the TV had a Super Nintendo with F-Zero on it! I remember absolutely nothing else about that trip, but I remember staying up late with my cousin taking turns playing that exhilarating, mesmerizing, colorful game. I was absolutely terrible at it, but that did not stop me from absolutely loving it.

Fast forward to now, and I find myself making Star Racer. The inspiration is clear on its face. It tries to evoke nostalgic feelings using pixel art and 16-bit music. But for me, the thing I try to come back to, beyond any of the presentation, is whether it makes me feel even one iota of the pure fun and joy I had playing so many years ago. It is so hard to create something and allow yourself to really feel it without bias. But I do think that Star Racer reaches that threshold I need to feel good about the direction of the game.

I also look at other indicators. I've read every comment, looked at how many backers we have, how many wishlists we've gotten, spoken with people in the Discord, and I suspect that I've been able to connect to that sense of joy in some of you as well.

So now at the end of this Kickstarter, I just want to say a big THANK YOU SO MUCH! You all have helped make it possible for me to execute on this vision I have to spark joy in people when they play this game.

I am so excited to take this game beyond the Kickstarter and finish it. There is still work to be done, but I am confident we will get there so much faster because of your help!

✨Star Racer Forever!✨

-Brennan
